text.description: Gentle walk-up on tundra slopes in the Mosquito Range; one of the easiest Centennial 13ers.
Long ridge and talus ascent in the Sangre de Cristos; a side trip to the Iron Nipple is optional.
Straightforward ridge walk, normally strung together with American and Niagara peaks.
Remote Chicago Basin objective reached by train; the final slopes are loose.

text.overview: Less intimidating than its appearance, running directly up the peak's tall north ridge to the top. Firm rock tilted around 45 degrees; mostly Class 3 moves, with a few Class 4 steps thrown in.

text.description: Steep grass and talus ridge above Lake Creek near Twin Lakes.

text.overview: Maroon Peak's easiest way up, yet long and very loose: a 2,800 ft grind up ledgy Class 3 slopes to the south ridge, a tiring traverse beneath Point 13,753, a scree gully and ledge onto the southwest face, then a choice of lines to the top.
The standard way up Missouri Mountain: up Missouri Gulch to its head, west over tundra and talus to a saddle, then along a narrow, somewhat exposed ridge path to the summit.

text.description: Long approach to a high basin followed by a ridge scramble with some Class 3 moves in the Sangre de Cristos.
Short, easy tundra climb from Kite Lake; commonly done with the Decalibron group.
Tundra ridge off the Argentine Pass road near Georgetown with some rocky sections.
Steady climb with considerable loose talus on the upper ridge, usually done with neighboring Quail Mountain.

text.overview: The standard hike up Massive: a long, nontechnical trail route up the broad east side, finishing along the crest from the 13,900-ft col that separates the main summit from South Massive.

text.description: Steady grassy and talus slopes above Halfmoon Creek.
Short, mostly walking ascent along the Continental Divide ridge from the pass, with a bit of rocky stepping near the top.

text.overview: Oxford is usually climbed as an add-on from Mount Belford, dropping east along the connecting ridge to a saddle near 13,490 ft and climbing back up to Oxford. The return over Belford adds a lot of extra vertical, so many parties camp high in Elkhead Basin.

The easiest way up Shavano: a trail climbs through forest and above tree line, staying on the north edge of the basin below the Angel snowfield, to the 13,330-ft col below the top; 0.6 mile of talus then leads north to the summit.
